description: Routes legitimately exempt from per-request Idempotency-Key enforcement (must have alternative dedup or be low-risk).

entries.justification: Session-bootstrap endpoint: sets the active-org cookie based on (userId, orgId). The effect is deterministic and naturally idempotent — replays produce identical cookie state with no DB writes. Idempotency-Key would add friction to a UI selection flow without changing dedup semantics.

SAGE Phase 8A recipient claim: CAS state transition (issued->active), not a repeated mutation. Idempotency is enforced by the unique invitation_token_hash constraint in the DB, not by an Idempotency-Key header. One-time token semantics make header-based dedup inapplicable.

SAGE Phase 8A recipient download: access_count is atomically incremented per-grant; the budget ceiling is the idempotency control. No DB-level dedup key would change the download semantics; the grant's max_accesses field is the governing constraint.
SAGE Phase 8A recipient acknowledgment: idempotent by unique event_id in sage_delivery_receipt (on conflict do nothing). Idempotency-Key header pattern does not apply to recipient-session operations.

Protected SAGE scheduler endpoint. Each attempt is claimed from the durable outbox with a fenced lease and uses a stable provider idempotency key, so replaying the scheduler request cannot create a second issuance or a second live claim.
